text: A machine learning accelerator is only as useful as the software that drives it. Before a language model can serve a single request on new hardware, every operation inside it has to be mapped onto the chip: matrix multiplications are split into tiles that fit the compute engines, intermediate results are placed in on-chip memory, and the numerical output is compared against a trusted reference until the two agree. This work is called model enablement. It sits between the compiler team, who decide how instructions are scheduled, and the customers, who only care that their model returns the same answers faster and at a lower cost. A good enablement engineer therefore needs two habits. The first is to measure everything, because an optimization that has not been measured is only a guess. The second is to check accuracy at every step, because a fast model that gives the wrong answer is worse than a slow one. In practice the day is spent reading profiles, moving data between layouts, and asking whether one more copy can be removed from the inner loop.
